biblical_reference.note: In the Bible, the name Eph is most notably associated with Ephraim, one of the twelve tribes of Israel. Ephraim is identified as the son of Joseph and Asenath, and is described as the elder brother of Manasseh. Ephraim is also referred to as 'the house of Joseph' or 'the house of Israel'. The territory allotted to the tribe of Ephraim includes the area around Bethel and Shechem.

data.cultural_impact: The name Eph hold historical ties to ancient Israel and Judea. It was the name of a major city mentioned numerous times in the Old and New Testaments, Ephesus. Throughout history, the name Eph has been used not only as a given name, but also as a surname, particularly among Christian communities.
data.spiritual_significance: In Christianity, the name Eph represents spiritual openness and fruitfulness. The Old Testament reference to Ephraim, one of Joseph's sons, holds special significance as a symbol of multiplicity, fruitfulness, and divine grace. Additionally, the New Testament reference to Ephesus, a city where St. Paul preached and conversion took place, reinforces the idea of spiritual growth and openness to God. Therefore, the name Eph carries a spiritual importance, calling its bearer to embrace the Divine and bear fruit in their lives.
